reviews.comment: Acct327 is one of the most difficult classes as a whole within Mays, but Dr. Twedt really made this class very doable. I found Acct229 so much harder than 327. Just go to class, have a solid study group, and look at the slides and you will do well. He is easily the best professor for Acct 327. Take him like do not hesitate at all.
reviews.ratingTags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor with great lectures. For exams and quizzes, you honestly just need to focus almost completely on the notes (take notes on the extra things he may say, but not have on the notes already). The book is not really needed, besides using it to do practice problems that he recommends. Only con was that there was not much practice to do.

I failed 327 twice, twedt was my last try and honestly, the best experience. he doesnt teach as many concepts as the other professors.  his quizzes are in class every week and you will do well if you memorize his slides and rework the problems. 2 exams and the final is cumulative. for exams, literally memorize lecture slides. guaranteed A

Brady Twedt is the easiest professor to take for ACCT 327. His exams are much less focused on small, intricate details than other professors that teach the class and more centered around the theory/broader concepts and principles. 

If you go to every class and study, it should be a pretty easy A. I would suggest that finance majors take this class

Best professor for ACCT 327! His quizzes and exams were strictly based on the slides which he prints out for students to take notes in class. He does a great job relating concepts to real world deals and scenarios which made his lectures actually very interesting.

Got a C in 229 and an A in this class. Brady is awesome and super fair. Go to class, take notes and study the ppts religiously. Exams aren't too bad at all and there's weekly quizzes based on stuff straight from the ppts. (he lets you do a few group quizzes and had an attendance quiz too). Recommend for sure!

Prof Twedt is the best professor you can get for ACCT. I was so nervous to take this class, but he genuinely cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. If you can try to go to his office hours and participate in class. All of his tests and quizzes are directly from the notes. The class is just hard in general but he makes it easier!
The accounting 327 goat! Brady is the best!

I am awful at accounting and did terrible in 229. I was super nervous to take 327 just because of how hard I heard it was. Prof Twedt makes the class so much more enjoyable and actually makes sense. There are in class quizzes every Thursday that are a little tougher because you genuinely need to take the time to study. Looks at slides only for test

i love brady! he's a great teacher and down to earth (even tho he has a phd he wants us to call him brady lol). cares about his students and their success, which makes 327 okay. can't speak about other profs but his class is probably easier. doesn't give many study resources but go to si and office hours, and ask questions! take him if you can.

Twedt is a great ACCT327 professor. Most 327 profs are known for grading and lecturing very difficultly but Twedt is straightforward, fair, and kind. I enjoyed him as a person and the tests were very similar to the in class notes. If you study and do practice problems you will have no problem getting a B or higher in his class.
One of the best professors I've had. Very engaging lectures and very competent. Taught the material very well and made one of the hardest classes here not so bad.

engaging teaching style, doesn't make you feel dumb for asking questions (very important imo). probably easier than other profs but not many study resources. most of your grade is from 2 tests and the final, and there are also 10 quizzes (drops 2 lowest). curves grades at the end. super funny, genuinely cares about his students and is a great guy!

Prof. Twedt is a fair professor for ACCT 327. His class is easier then the other professors but takes effort to receive a B or A. Not too many practice materials available for the exams, reworking the notes is the best option. The course is comprised of 3 tests (2 midterms and a final) along with quiz's. If you have the chance, take this professor!

He's genuinely a great guy, and I loved taking his class. I had him his first year at A&M and it was easier than other professors but could be different now. Only thing I didn't like about the class was his notes for students was poorly done.
